title: Finite closed intersections and their étale stalk models
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $n\geq0$, and let $D_j\hookrightarrow X$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] for $0\leq j<n$. For $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ set $Z=\mathop{\times}_{j\in J,X}D_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with $Z=X$ if $J=\varnothing$. Then the canonical morphism $i:Z\to X$ is a closed immersion and $Z$ is locally Noetherian. On every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A'\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], if $D_j\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A'/I'_j)$, then $Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A'/\sum_{j\in J}I'_j)$ over $U$. For $z\in Z$, put $x=i(z)$, choose such an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A'\ni x$, and put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $I=(\sum_{j\in J}I'_j)A$ (the image of the ideal of $Z$ in $A$, independent of $U$), so $\mathcal O_{Z,z}=A/I$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. For every étale $v:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $w\in W$ with $v(w)=x$, put $B=\mathcal O_{W,w}$. Then $B$ is a Noetherian local ring, $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}B\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $B/IB$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring. There is a unique point $\widetilde w\in Z\times_XW$ over $w$; its local ring is $B/IB$, and the stalk map $\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to\mathcal O_{Z\times_XW,\widetilde w}$ identifies with the natural flat local homomorphism $A/I\to B/IB$ [def-weil-flat-morphism].

proof.text: Work over an arbitrary affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$. Restriction of fibre products to these opens is the open-fibre-product identification. Enumerate $J$ and induct on the number of factors, with coordinate ring $R/L$ where $L$ is the sum of the ideals already used. The empty product is $U$, with $L=0$. Adding $D_j$ gives $\operatorname{Spec}((R/L)\otimes_R(R/I'_j))$. Apply the tensor-quotient formula with $B=R/L$: its ring is $(R/L)/(I'_j(R/L))=R/(L+I'_j)$. The last equality follows directly: the inverse image of $I'_j(R/L)$ consists of $L+I'_j$, and both quotient maps send $r$ to its class. Thus all identifications respect the maps from $R$ and the projections. This proves the asserted affine formula for every $U$. The affine characterization of closed immersions now gives that $i$ is closed.

source.place: Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); Morphisms Tag 01QO; Algebra quotient calculation

proof.text: Choose the affine cover $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ of $X$ with $R_a$ Noetherian supplied by local Noetherianity. The preceding step gives an affine cover of $Z$ by quotient rings of the $R_a$; a quotient is a finite-type algebra (zero polynomial variables), so the finite-type Noetherian theorem makes all these rings Noetherian. Hence $Z$ is locally Noetherian. Also $v$ is unramified, and the definition of unramified includes locally of finite type. Over each $U_a$, the definition of locally of finite type supplies an affine cover of $v^{-1}U_a$ by spectra of finite-type $R_a$-algebras $C$. These $C$ are Noetherian by the same theorem. Choose such a chart containing $w$; the affine-stalk identification gives $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$, which is Noetherian by localization. It is a local ring because it is a scheme stalk. This argument uses the chosen Noetherian cover, not an unproved assertion about every affine open.

Fix $z$, $x=i(z)$ and an arbitrary affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$ as in the statement. Write $K=\sum_{j\in J}I'_j$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $x$. Since $z$ corresponds to a prime of $R/K$, $K\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The affine-stalk and quotient-localization identifications give $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal O_{Z,z}=R_{\mathfrak p}/KR_{\mathfrak p}=A/I$. Their maps are the actual stalk maps: on fractions the map sends $r/s$ to $\bar r/\bar s$. Its kernel is therefore $I=KR_{\mathfrak p}$. In particular $I$ is independent of the affine neighbourhood, being the kernel of $i_z^\sharp$. The ideal sheaf of $i$ restricts on this chart to $\widetilde K$, and the associated-module stalk-localization theorem identifies its stalk with $K_{\mathfrak p}$, whose image in $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $KR_{\mathfrak p}=I$. Also $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$.

Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the stalk map of $v$ at $w$. It is local by the definition of a scheme morphism, hence $IB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. The quotient-local-structure theorem gives that $B/IB$ is nonzero and local. It is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian theorem, applied to the quotient of the Noetherian ring $B$. The structural map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ factors through $U$ with ring map $R\to A\to B$. The affine fibre-product and tensor-quotient formulas yield $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}B=\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}B$: extending $K$ through its localization $I$ generates the same ideal in $B$, since the denominators in $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ map to units in $B$. Reassociation of these pullbacks follows from their universal property.

For the point and stalk assertions choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq v^{-1}U$ of $w$, with prime $\mathfrak q$ and ring map $\psi:R\to C$. On this open the pullback $P=Z\times_XW$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C/KC)$, by the same two affine formulas. The inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ is $\mathfrak p$, so $KC\subseteq\mathfrak q$. There is exactly one prime of $C/KC$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$, namely $\mathfrak q/KC$: an ideal of a quotient is determined by its inverse image. Thus exactly one point $\widetilde w$ of $P$ lies over $w$, since any such point lies in this open. Its local ring is $(C/KC)_{\mathfrak q/KC}=C_{\mathfrak q}/KC_{\mathfrak q}=B/IB$ by quotient-localization. This also identifies the local quotient map with the stalk map from $W$.

The projection $P\to Z$ is the base change of the etale map $v$, hence etale. By the definitions of etale and flat morphisms its stalk map at $\widetilde w$ is flat and local. The affine projection formulas and the formula for stalk maps of spectrum morphisms identify it explicitly: for $r\in R$ and $s\notin\mathfrak p$ it sends $\bar r/\bar s$ in $(R/K)_{\mathfrak p/K}=A/I$ to $\overline{\psi(r)}/\overline{\psi(s)}$ in $(C/KC)_{\mathfrak q/KC}=B/IB$. These fractions exhaust the source; thus it is exactly the quotient map induced by $\varphi$, with no choice of a different algebra structure. This proves the final assertion. When $J$ is empty all sums and extended ideals are zero, $Z=X$, $P=W$, and these formulas reduce to $A\to B$; if $Z$ is empty the assertions quantified over $z$ are vacuous.

Every point over w lies in this open, so the point is globally unique, and its local ring is C_q/KC_q = B/IB.
